theses.headline: West African copper/gold-belt miners (DRC, Zambia, Mali) outperform over the next 9-12 months as the base/precious metals super-cycle that co-moves with South Sudan and Mozambique conflict intensity continues its 12-month rally.
theses.rationale: The firm's own correlation work shows South Sudan and Mozambique conflict metrics tracking global copper, silver, gold and platinum prices at r~0.5-0.7 -- most plausibly because a shared global liquidity/commodity super-cycle is driving both metal prices and the security spending/violence economics of resource-linked frontier states simultaneously. Copper is up 39.9% and gold up 20.8% over 12 months, confirming that cycle is live. Layered onto this are country-level findings of continued large-scale extractive capital presence even amid instability: Barrick's Loulo-Gounkoto complex in Mali survived a provisional-administration dispute and reverted to Barrick control, DRC's Kamoa-Kakula (Ivanhoe) and Port of Banana concession continue attracting large-ticket financing, and Zambia is targeting over 1 million tonnes of copper output in 2026 backed by ~$10bn in mining capital deepening. This is a super-cycle beta trade expressed through the miners physically present in the highest-conflict-correlated geographies, not a claim that conflict causes the metal rally.
supporting_signals: South Sudan conflict/protest/severity metrics correlate r~0.5-0.7 with copper, silver, gold, platinum, aluminum at zero lag (cross-cutting insight)
Mozambique conflict/violence leads copper prices by up to 1 month at r~0.69-0.72 (cross-cutting insight)
Copper +39.9% and Gold +20.8% over 12 months (Yahoo Finance monthly closes, 2026-07)
Barrick's Loulo-Gounkoto (Mali) provisional-administration-to-recovery template and Zambia's $10bn four-year mining capital deepening plus Luanshya redevelopment (country findings)
risks: The correlation is explicitly flagged as likely confounded by a common global macro/dollar-liquidity factor, not a direct causal African-conflict-to-price channel -- if the metals cycle turns, the African conflict linkage offers no hedge
Sahel and DRC operational risk (nationalization, contract renegotiation, insurgency near assets) can impair individual miners regardless of the metal price backdrop
FQVLF and IVPAF are thin, foreign-listed, and carry currency/liquidity spread risk versus the diversified miner ETFs

Reverse causality is plausible (rising metal prices raising the value of contested territory, fueling conflict) rather than conflict driving prices, which weakens the trade's directional logic if used as a leading indicator

theses.headline: Kenyan capital-markets and fintech names outperform on a 3-9 month horizon as the historical unrest-to-investment-inflow lag plays out following recent instability.
theses.rationale: The firm's statistical work finds Kenyan conflict, protest, and political-violence events each correlate at r=0.575 with investment_events three months later across a robust 63-month sample -- the strongest-sample finding in the dataset -- consistent with a pattern of post-unrest stabilization financing or election-cycle donor confidence returning a quarter after disruption. This dovetails with concrete, current-dated momentum: Nairobi's push for NIFC status with 15 newly certified firms and a targeted $200m in fresh capital into digital finance, AI and carbon markets, plus the NSE hitting an all-time market-cap high of KSh3.73 trillion in H1 2026, and DFC's continued direct lending into Kenyan fintech (M-Kopa $51.0M, Mogo Auto $10.0M). The thesis is that any near-term unrest spike should be read as a contrarian entry signal for Kenya-linked financial exposure rather than a pure risk-off cue, given the empirical lag structure.
supporting_signals: Kenyan conflict/protest/political-violence events each correlate r=0.575 with investment_events at a 3-month lag, n=63 months (cross-cutting insight)
NSE market capitalization hit an all-time high of KSh3.73 trillion in H1 2026 (Kenyan Wall Street, cited July 2026)
Nairobi NIFC certification of 15 new firms and a targeted $200M in fresh capital across digital finance, AI and carbon markets (Breaking Kenya News, July 3, 2026)
DFC direct-lending pattern into Kenyan fintech/embedded finance (M-Kopa Kenya $51.0M, Mogo Auto $10.0M, Pezesha $500K technical assistance, FY2024 filings)
risks: The three instability series are collinear (identical r and lag) -- this is one signal, not three independent confirmations, and may simply reflect Kenya's fixed election calendar clustering both unrest and investment announcements

theses.headline: Guinea-linked bauxite/iron-ore infrastructure and power plays benefit over 12-18 months as Simandou-driven power-sector buildout accelerates state and multilateral co-investment.
theses.rationale: Guinea's country findings show a concrete, dated policy push -- PM Amadou Oury Bah's June 28, 2026 call for power-sector transformation explicitly tied to 'Simandou 2040' -- backed by real bankable structures: the 180MW Kankan-Siguiri-Kouroussa-Boké-Linsan solar PV project and the earlier $76.5M Boké solar park (both World Bank PPI-tracked), plus continued private telecom capital appetite via Orange Guinea's $227.4M brownfield ICT portfolio despite mining-sector contract disputes. Rio Tinto's direct Simandou iron-ore exposure makes it the most literal instrument available for this specific corridor, while the broader steel/iron-ore demand read-through and diversified-miner ETFs offer diluted but liquid alternatives. This is a long-dated infrastructure-buildout thesis riding an explicit government mandate rather than a commodity-price call, distinct from the separate iron-ore price trend (-7.7% over 3 months, roughly flat over 12 months).

theses.headline: Southern African utility-scale renewable and battery-storage developers see continued bankable deal flow over the next 12 months as South Africa's sovereign-upgrade cycle lowers infrastructure financing costs.
theses.rationale: South Africa shows the deepest, most recent PPI-tracked renewable pipeline in the dataset -- Oya Energy Hybrid ($693.4M), Oasis 1 ($386.6M), Mogobe BESS ($170.0M), and Virginia Solar Park ($248.0M), all active 2024 -- against a backdrop of back-to-back sovereign rating upgrades from Moody's (May 2026), S&P (June 1, 2026) and Fitch (June 5, 2026) tied to a third consecutive primary fiscal surplus. Improving sovereign credit conditions directly lower the cost of capital for the exact public-private infrastructure vehicles financing this pipeline, creating a self-reinforcing loop between macro credibility and project bankability. DFC's parallel $50.0M equity stake in TechMet Phalaborwa Rare Earths signals Western development finance is also underwriting adjacent critical-minerals infrastructure in the same country, reinforcing the broad-based capital-formation story.

theses.headline: Mozambique-linked LNG value-chain majors and connectivity beneficiaries rally over 12-24 months as TotalEnergies' Mozambique LNG restart and ExxonMobil's expected Rovuma FID unlock a multi-year hydrocarbons capex cycle, reinforced by Tanzania's regional shipping-connectivity surge.
theses.rationale: TotalEnergies' restart of its $20 billion Mozambique LNG project (40% built, first gas targeted 2029) and an expected ExxonMobil FID on the $30 billion Rovuma LNG project by September 2026 represent one of the largest committed hydrocarbons capex cycles in the country findings, explicitly requiring ancillary logistics, workforce housing, and services investment per President Chapo's June 2026 statements. This is reinforced by DFC/World Bank PPI commitments concentrated in power transmission tied to the LNG corridor ($450M Chimuara-Nacala transmission, $270M Namaacha wind), and by Tanzania's standout +16.2pt year-on-year UNCTAD Liner Shipping Connectivity Index gain -- the third-largest mover globally -- suggesting the wider East African coast is absorbing rising trade and project-logistics volume alongside the Mozambican LNG buildout. TotalEnergies is the only verified instrument with direct, named Mozambique LNG exposure.

theses.headline: Global cocoa-exposed agribusiness processors and cocoa futures remain directionally supported over the next 6 months as West African (Ghana/Ivory Coast) supply-side financing continues even as cocoa prices retrace from extreme highs.
theses.rationale: Cocoa is the standout commodity mover in the dataset -- up 60.4% over 3 months even after a -38.6% 12-month decline, indicating a sharp near-term price reversal precisely in the crop most concentrated in Ghana and Ivory Coast, the two dominant global producers. Ghana's recurring, multi-year COCOBOD syndicated financing facility (Bank of China/ICBC tranches within a $1.3-1.5bn facility, persisting across multiple crop seasons) demonstrates that structured receivables financing around cocoa continues uninterrupted, while Ivory Coast's National Development Plan explicitly targets agriculture within its $209bn 2030 investment program with 70% intended from private capital. The combination of a violent price move and durable production-financing infrastructure supports a tactical, shorter-horizon thesis on cocoa-linked exposure, though the extreme volatility (from -38.6% to +60.4% inside a year) argues for caution on conviction and horizon.

risks: Extreme volatility (-38.6% to +60.4% within 12 months) makes this a high-variance tactical trade, not a stable structural thesis -- the reversal could itself mean-revert further against the position

theses.headline: Niger and broader Sahel uranium/critical-minerals producers see rising exploration and fiscal momentum over 12 months as state-directed mining revenue and exploration investment accelerate.
theses.rationale: Niger's country findings show concrete, dated fiscal momentum in mining: sector revenue nearly tripled to CFA18 billion and exploration investment rose to over CFA14 billion in 2025 per the Mines Minister's May 4, 2026 statement, alongside an improving fiscal position as 80% of oil revenues were restored to the budget mid-2026 following repayment of a $400 million oil-backed loan. Niger is a globally significant uranium producer, and the URA ETF's explicit exposure note flags Niger/Namibia producer exposure, making it the most direct available instrument for this state-driven extractives-tightening story. This is an early-stage, state-control-driven thesis rather than a liquid market signal -- exploration and licensing momentum do not guarantee near-term production or price capture, and uranium prices themselves are down 27.5% over 3 months despite a modest 12-month gain.

theses.headline: Zambian and DRC copperbelt capital deepening supports a structural 12-18 month re-rating in copper miners as both governments push production targets well above prior levels amid a still-rising 12-month copper price trend.
theses.rationale: This is the most concrete, non-conflict-correlation-dependent copper thesis in the intelligence set: Zambia's Mines Minister cites approximately $10 billion in mining-sector capital deepening over four years plus the $710 million Luanshya copper mine redevelopment targeting August 2026 output, explicitly aimed at exceeding 1 million tonnes of copper production in 2026, while DRC's Kamoa-Kakula complex and the $1.2bn Port of Banana seaport concession provide the export-logistics backbone for rising DRC copper volumes. This sits against a genuinely strong commodity backdrop -- copper +7.6% over 3 months and +39.9% over 12 months, the strongest sustained industrial-metal trend in the dataset -- giving the production-side buildout a supportive price environment rather than one it must fight against, unlike the uranium or iron-ore theses above.

risks: A reversal in the global copper cycle (e.g., China demand slowdown or dollar strength) would remove the price tailwind supporting both the production buildout's economics and the equities
